briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and Google Gemini 3 push multi-agent frontiers as compute shortages intensify

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AGI race accelerates with frontier labs releasing advanced reasoning models while regulatory scrutiny grows over safety. Funding remains robust but compute constraints are bottlenecking smaller players. Prompt injection and multi-agent security emerge as critical deployment risks.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed o4 with enhanced multi-agent orchestration; Anthropic released Claude 4 Opus; Google DeepMind launched Gemini 3; Meta open-sourced Llama 4 405B; xAI shipped Grok-3; DeepSeek unveiled R2. Multi-agent coordination benchmarks show 40% gains over prior generations.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New EU AI Act enforcement guidelines target agentic systems; researchers disclosed novel jailbreaks in o3.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA H200 shipments ramp to 1.2M units quarterly; Microsoft and Oracle announce joint 200k H100 cluster in Texas; TSMC 2nm AI chips enter volume production; energy demands force data center delays in Europe.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will multi-agent security protocols like dynamic dialect negotiation become mandatory for all frontier deployments by 2027?
